representation: A fixed four-bar skewed raw population histogram above a seven-bar histogram of sample means whose heights depend on n through a 1/sqrt(n) spread, centered on a dashed population mean.
motion: As n grows, the middle sample-mean bars rise and the outer bars fall, so the sampling distribution narrows into a bell; the raw histogram never changes.
controls: slider for sample size n from 1 to 36
checkpoints: bottom bars are means, not raw data
raw data does not become normal
spread shrinks with n around the population mean
misconceptionTest: The raw bars remain fixed and skewed as n changes, so the original data does not become normal. The CLT is about the distribution of sample means, which centers near the population mean and narrows as n grows.
accessibility: Alt text, keyboard slider, separated top and bottom histograms, and a textual summary distinguishing raw data from the sampling distribution.
